The event store did not adopt a dedicated cache layer like Redis. Instead, the team decided against introducing Redis as a lookup cache for the event store based on measured performance and workload characteristics.

The decision was made after evaluating the working set size and read-latency requirements. Measurements showed that the hot working set comfortably fits in application memory, eliminating the need for an external cache [Data: session-044 (18)]. The team explicitly rejected the Redis proposal from session-040 due to the lack of demonstrated read-latency bottlenecks [Data: adr-009 (1), session-040 (17)].

The focus shifted to addressing write contention, which led to the migration from SQLite to PostgreSQL to handle concurrent writes effectively [Data: adr-007 (0), production-notes (14)].
